title: A hydrogen-like ion's binding
hook: Change nuclear charge number and predict binding-energy magnitude.
misconception: binding-energy magnitude doubles when nuclear charge number doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply abs(E_n) = 13.6 Z² eV/n² to compare binding-energy magnitude when nuclear charge number changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With the nonrelativistic Bohr model of a one-electron ion at fixed principal quantum number, abs(E_n) = 13.6 Z² eV/n². When nuclear charge number doubles, binding-energy magnitude becomes 4 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model abs(E_n) = 13.6 Z² eV/n²; scaling exponent 2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider the nonrelativistic Bohr model of a one-electron ion at fixed principal quantum number, with a nonzero initial result. If nuclear charge number triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on binding-energy magnitude?
recall.why: Apply abs(E_n) = 13.6 Z² eV/n² under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 9.
